verdict_notes: Every PASS below is read from a recorded result of the named check in the named file; the digests are computed from the committed files (`SHA256SUMS` seals every file in this directory, raw logs included).
A browser engine, architecture, or scanner that was not run is UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Where a result is FAIL the failing evidence is in the linked file and in section 5.

findings.title: TestSecurityUIBrowser/recovery-reveal-phone fails on Firefox (SH-9a FAIL)
findings.detail: `browsers/firefox-desktop.log` and `browsers/firefox-phone.log`: `TestSecurityUIBrowser/firefox/recovery-reveal-phone/{light,dark}` fail with `replacement code: Hide the code button is below the fold after focus (... Hide the code button: top 852 ...)` at the 844 px phone viewport; every other scenario passes on Firefox, and the whole matrix passes on Chromium and WebKit (desktop and phone). A temporary, uncommitted diagnostic showed why: on that page the Hide button is disabled until the acknowledgement is ticked, `focus()` on a disabled button does nothing, and Firefox lays this card out taller than the other engines, so the button stays at y = 852 with `scrollY = 0` (document height 1417). The scenario was added at P1.18.4 and hosted CI runs Chromium only, so it had never run on Firefox. Whether the layout or the scenario should change is the P1.18.4 owner's decision; the test was not weakened. The browsers are therefore **not** all green and the criterion stays FAIL.

findings.title: Start-up transient: about 100 MB resident for 2.5 minutes after every start
findings.detail: technical-decisions.md 10.2 states the idle budget as "after startup" without a duration. In steady state the service is well inside it (27.8 MB after a first start, 33.3 MB when configured, 27.2 MB after a restart; `vm-amd64/release.json`, `footprint.idle`), and `REL-FOOT-SETTLE-*` passes. But every start (first start, restart, SIGKILL restart) first holds about 100 MB (100.55 MB peak after the first start, 98.81 MB after a restart) until 145-155 s, i.e. roughly twice the budget for two and a half minutes; the same figures were measured on both hosted CPUs (98-99 MB, settled at 140-160 s). It reproduces natively with the container's environment: with the SMTP relay configured, one heap allocation of about 64 MiB happens 85 ms after start (`GODEBUG=gctrace=1`: `94->94->88 MB`), and Go returns it to the OS only after the runtime's 2-minute forced collection. Not asserted here: which code path allocates it. A follow-up in the product (release the memory after the one-time work) would remove the transient; the harness records the whole curve and gates on the settle.

findings.title: Intermittent fail-closed refusals of granted calls under the approved workload on the slow VM daemon
findings.detail: `REL-LOAD-STABLE` is its own result because it is not a memory figure. On the VM (4 vCPU, Docker 29.9.3 with the containerd snapshotter; 1.8 ms 4 KiB fsync, sequential allowed call p50 181-208 ms) the workload of 10 REST pollers + 10 real-MCP sessions + 5 follow streams sometimes receives `403 forbidden` for calls that the policy allows: `safety_unverified` (the Docker backend proof is invalid; every operational call is refused before any dispatch) and, less often, `default_deny`. Observed on the same image content: 0 errors in the final run and in `diagnostics/vm-run-0d8b431-full.json`; 190 REST / 228 MCP non-200 answers in `diagnostics/vm-run-1a01db9-full.json`; 38 REST + 8 `default_deny` + 34 `safety_unverified` in `diagnostics/vm-diag-loop-1.json`; 142 REST + 5 `default_deny` + 165 `safety_unverified` in `diagnostics/vm-diag-loop-2.json` (diagnostic runs repeat the matrix and the load only). The hosted runners (4 vCPU, 16 GB, Docker 28.0.4 with overlay2, 0.03-0.15 ms fsync, sequential allowed call p50 61 ms amd64 / 72 ms arm64) served 1022 + 1021 REST and 2259 MCP calls without one error on amd64 and 932 + 932 and 1999 on arm64, in 61 s, REST p50 96 / 123 ms. In the failing runs the usage store held more `allowed` outcomes than the client saw successes (for example 141 against 128 for `rel-load1 container:logs`), which the harness reports as a failed exact-count check and then re-baselines so later stages stay exact. The service log shows only the initial `docker backend verified` line, so a transition to UNVERIFIED is not logged. Not asserted: the cause (the documented per-admission inventory recheck and supersession of older verifications under concurrency is the likely area). The final VM run is clean; the result is intermittent on this daemon, which is why it is recorded here and not hidden by that run.

findings.title: Sign-in and setup raise the resident set to about 180 MB (outside the benchmark workload)
findings.detail: `footprint.idle[configured].VmHWM_process_lifetime` is 178.07 MB on the VM (178.9 and 181.8 MB on the hosted runners): the setup, identity and matrix sign-ins (Argon2id, 64 MiB each) push the process above the 150 MB load budget briefly. The benchmark workload (API/MCP clients and log streams) contains no human sign-in and its measured peak is 41-43 MB with the high-water mark reset at the start of the window, so the budget is met as defined; a burst of sign-ins during load is not covered by this workload.

findings.title: The restore manifest's `inactive_credentials` counts the installation's inactive records, not only the imported ones
findings.detail: After a **clean** restore the manifest reports `agent_credentials 0` and `authenticators 2`; the two authenticators are the ones the restore itself retired locally (`restore report credentials_stripped: true`, no imported credential). docs/backup-restore.md says a clean archive carries no credential, which is true; the manifest field name suggests otherwise. The harness asserts the bearer-credential count and the report flag, not the sum.

findings.title: Measurement notes
findings.detail: (a) The hosted runners' `docker` buildx driver cannot export OCI, so on them the compressed image size is an **estimate** (every layer of `docker save` gzip-compressed at level 6; 12.29 MB amd64 and 11.66 MB arm64); on the VM the real OCI export gives 12 418 706 bytes and the estimator was calibrated against it at 0.15% on the same image (12 400 226 against 12 418 702 bytes). (b) The crash is a SIGKILL delivered to the service process from the host: `docker kill` is not used because the daemon treats it as a manual stop and never applies the restart policy. (c) The `--skip` option of the harness exists for diagnostics only; the final run skipped nothing (`stage_seconds` has no `skipped`).
